Rules: real_exam/TEACHING_STYLE_GUIDE.md R1-R35 (no 'which way is better' verdict) + NITZAN_RHYTHM_DELIVERY.md P1-P13. Calm preset on the question reading and plain calculations.

slides.say: In the figure, each vertex of rectangle A B C D is the center of a circle with a radius of two centimeters. Point O is the center of a circle that is tangent to the four quarter circles, and to sides A D and B C. What is the area of rectangle A B C D, in square centimeters?
The area of a rectangle is length times width. The short side, A B, is four, and it's written in the figure. So we need the long side, A D.
Along A D, the first part is a radius of the quarter circle at A, so it's two. The last part is a radius of the quarter circle at D, so it's also two.
at: the first part is a radius

slides.say: We want to estimate that middle part. Let's draw helper lines to get bounds from the given lengths. We won't need to calculate the missing length exactly.
But wait. On the exam, a figure is not necessarily drawn to scale. So can I estimate from the figure?

No, we shouldn't measure the sketch. Let's use the lengths. The middle circle touches the top and bottom sides, four apart. Its diameter is four, so its radius is two. Draw a line from A to O, joining two touching circles' centers.

The corner circle has radius two, and the middle circle has radius two. The circles touch from the outside, so A O is two plus two, four. From O, draw a perpendicular to side A B. Call its foot H. O is two below the top side, so A H is two. Now A H O is a right triangle, with hypotenuse four and one leg two.
at: A O is two plus two, four
hypotenuse four and one leg two

slides.say: Call O H x. By Pythagoras, x squared plus two squared is four squared. Four squared is sixteen, and two squared is four. Subtract four, and x squared is twelve. We only need bounds for x, not its exact root.
Three squared is nine, below twelve. Four squared is sixteen, above twelve. So the positive length x is more than three and less than four.
at: more than three and less than four

slides.say: The same construction on the right has the same hypotenuse, four, and the same vertical leg, two. So its horizontal length is also x. The whole rectangle is x plus x across. That's why A D is two x, not just x.
Each x is between three and four. Double both bounds, and A D is between six and eight. We got that from the right triangles, not from measuring the picture.
at: A D is between six and eight

slides: This also explains the middle part we started with. A D is between six and eight. Take away the two radius pieces, two at each end, four altogether. The middle part is therefore between two and four. Either way, the full side A D is between six and eight.

slides.say: The area is four times A D. Four times six is twenty-four, and four times eight is thirty-two. So the area is between twenty-four and thirty-two, and it isn't equal to either one.
[pause] Now the choices. Choice number four, forty, is more than thirty-two. It's out.
Choice number three, thirty-two. The middle part is less than four, so the area is less than thirty-two. It's out too.

Choice number two, sixteen root two. The area has to be more than twenty-four. Sixteen times one and a half is sixteen plus eight, twenty-four. So to pass twenty-four, the root has to be more than one and a half.
at: Sixteen times one and a half

slides.say: But one and a half squared is two and a quarter, which is more than two. So root two is less than one and a half, and sixteen root two is less than twenty-four. It's out.
at: But one and a half squared
sixteen root two is less than twenty-four

slides.say: Three choices are out, so choice number one, sixteen root three, is our answer.

Now let's go back to x squared is twelve. If you spot a square factor inside twelve, you can finish even sooner. Twelve is four times three. So the root of twelve is the root of four times the root of three: two root three. That's x. The whole long side is two x, so it's four root three. The other side is four. Four times four root three gives sixteen root three, choice number one, without checking all the other choices. If you don't spot the root shortcut, our bounds still give a safe way to eliminate them. I'll see you in the next question.
